passages.text: The manuscript series follows four connected threads. Papers 01--06 study positive and indefinite completions of fourth-order systems and the interaction problem. Papers 07--13 move to gauge reduction, causal BV--BFV transport, compact laboratories, observables, anomaly, and nonlinear continuation. Papers 14--18 study pure-Weyl black holes and the four-level ghost classification. Papers 19--22 separate physical assumptions from mathematical carriers through Mannheim gravity, gauge algebra, reverse foundations, and a Bateman--Turok counterfamily. Papers 98 and 99 provide physicist and general-audience entrances; Papers 90--92 and the computational supplements expose selected interfaces and verification details.

passages.text: Finite-harmonic nonlinear continuation and several obstruction branches are known without a complete bounded nonlinear cone. At one loop, strict pure Weyl has a nonzero local Euclidean BV anomaly. A formal shifting compensator repairs the tested identity only after enlarging the field content and counterterm space; it is therefore a result about a changed theory.
